info.title: Logis API
info.description:
Logis API: authentication, global search and custom asset views.

## Authentication and token rotation

1. `POST /auth/login` returns a bearer token that expires after 60 minutes without use.
2. Every authenticated request (except `logout` and `refresh`) rotates the token. The new token arrives in the
   `X-Refreshed-Token` response header. Whenever that header is present, replace the stored token.
   When it is absent, keep the current one.
3. The previous token keeps working for a 10 second grace period, so requests fired in parallel with the
   old token still succeed. Only one of them receives a new token.
4. `POST /auth/refresh` rotates explicitly and returns the new token in the body.
5. `POST /auth/logout` revokes the current token and its predecessor if it is still in its grace period.

In this Swagger UI the token is handled automatically. Login and refresh authorize the session, every
`X-Refreshed-Token` replaces the stored token, and logout clears it. Log in with `demo@logis.test` / `password`.

Every response, success or error, uses the same format: `{ success, data, message, meta }`.
The HTTP status tells the client what happened. The API allows 60 requests per minute.

tags.description: Login, token rotation, refresh, logout and the authenticated user.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Global search across the entities of the customers the user can see.

tags.name: Views
tags.description:
Custom views: saved columns and filters over assets, tickets, contracts or locations.
A user sees their own views and the public views of their own customer. Only the owner can change,
delete or set a view as default. A view the user cannot see answers 404.

post.summary: Log in with email and password

200.description: Token refreshed. The previous token keeps working during the grace period.

409.description: The token was already rotated by a concurrent request.

get.summary: Search tickets, assets, contracts and locations across the visible customers
get.description:
Searches each requested entity for `q` and returns, per entity, the newest matches up to `limit`,
the total number of matches and whether there are more.

The server decides which customers the user can see: their own customer and, when the user has the
sub-account permission, its sub-accounts. A user without a customer gets empty results.

| Entity | Searched fields (contains, case-insensitive) | Extra filter |
|---|---|---|
| `tickets` | subject, repair id, incident number | not deleted |
| `assets` | serial number, manufacturer, model | not deleted, any status |
| `contracts` | name | active only |
| `locations` | title, full address, city, state, postal code | — |

The term is matched literally: `%` and `_` are not wildcards. Results are cached for 5 minutes.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term, as valid UTF-8 text. Leading and trailing spaces are removed, and it must not be empty.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results per entity. Absent or empty means 5.

parameters.name: entities
parameters.description:
Entities to search, comma-separated (`entities=tickets,assets`). The array form
`entities[]=tickets&entities[]=assets` is accepted too. Duplicates and empty values are ignored.
All entities are searched when it is absent.

get.summary: List the views the user can see
get.description:
Returns the user's own views and the public views of the user's customer, ordered by title.
There is no pagination. A user without a customer gets an empty list.

post.description:
Creates a view owned by the user, for the user's customer. The columns and filters must belong to the
field catalog of the view type (see `ViewFilter`); otherwise the response is 422 with a message that
names the column or filter. A new view is never the default: use `set-default`. The response carries no data.

| View type | Fields |
|---|---|
| `my_assets` | id, serial_number, manufacturer, model, item_name, status, customer, contract, location, created_at, updated_at |
| `my_tickets` | id, repair_id, incident_number, subject, status, asset, customer, created_at, updated_at |
| `my_contracts` | id, name, status, customer, created_at, updated_at |
| `my_locations` | id, title, full_address, city, state, postal_code, customer, created_at, updated_at |

201.description: The view was created. Read it with `GET /views` or `GET /views/{id}`.

get.summary: Get the details of a view

put.description:
Replaces the title, description, columns, filters and `is_public` of a view. Only the owner can do it.
`view_type` can't change: it may be sent, but only with the current value. The same catalog rules as
creation apply, and an absent `is_public` means `false`.

delete.description: Deletes a view. Only the owner can do it. Deleting the default view leaves its type without a default.

post.description:
Returns one page of rows of the view's entity, with the view's columns and filters. The rows always belong
to the customers of the user who executes the view, never to the owner's: a public view shows each user
only their own data. A user without a customer gets no rows.

Pages are cursor-based: pass `meta.next_cursor` of a page as `cursor` to get the next one, with the same
sort. `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page. A cursor of another sort order is rejected with 422.
Results are cached for 5 minutes. An execution that runs longer than 5 seconds is stopped and answers 504.

Only these fields can be sorted: `id`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and the text or choice fields of the
entity's own table (not relations nor the nullable address fields of locations).

post.summary: Set a view as the default of its type
post.description:
Makes the view the owner's default for its type. The previous default of that owner and type stops being
the default in the same transaction. Setting the current default again changes nothing. Only the owner can
do it.

200.description: The view is now the default of its type

sanctum.description: Sanctum access token. When it is rotated, the new one arrives in the X-Refreshed-Token header.

XRefreshedToken.description: The rotated token. Replace the stored token with it. Absent when a concurrent request already rotated the token.

total.description: Number of matches, before the limit

has_more.description: Whether total is greater than the limit

data.description: One entry per requested entity, in the order tickets, assets, contracts, locations.

ViewFilter.description:
A filter on one field of the view type. Filters are combined with AND.

| Field type | Operators | Value |
|---|---|---|
| text | `eq`, `neq`, `contains` / `in`, `not_in` | 1 to 255 characters / a list of 1 to 100 |
| choice (`status` of assets and contracts) | `eq`, `neq` / `in`, `not_in` | one of the allowed values / a list |
| identifier (`id` and relations such as `location`, `contract`, `customer`, ticket `status`, `asset`) | `eq` / `in`, `not_in` | a positive integer id / a list |
| date (`created_at`, `updated_at`) | `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte` / `between` / `in_last_days` | a `Y-m-d` date / two dates / 0 to 365 days |

Dates are whole UTC days: `gt 2024-01-01` starts on 2024-01-02, `between` includes both days and
`in_last_days 0` is today. `contains` matches literally, `%` and `_` are not wildcards.

`user_filter` decides what the user who executes the view can do with the saved filters of that field:

| `user_filter` | The user can send |
|---|---|
| `restricted` | a subset of the saved values, with `eq` or `in` |
| `open` | any valid filter for the field, which replaces the saved ones |
| `locked` (default) | nothing: the saved filters always apply |

When a view is saved, all the filters of one field must share their `user_filter`, and a `restricted`
field has a single filter with `eq` or `in`. Otherwise the response is 422.

value.description: A string, an integer, or a list of them, depending on the operator.

user_filter.description: Optional. Absent or null means locked.

title.description: Unique among the views of the owner

is_public.description: Share the view with the users of the owner's customer

is_default.description: Whether this is the requesting user's default view of its type

is_public.description: Whether the view is shared with the users of its customer

is_owner.description: Whether the requesting user owns the view and can change it

columns.description: Fields shown by the view, in order

filters.description:
Filters of the user who executes the view, combined with AND. Each one follows the catalog rules of
`ViewFilter` and the `user_filter` of the saved filters of its field:

| Field | What happens |
|---|---|
| saved filter `restricted` | accepted if it uses `eq` or `in` with a subset of the saved values; it replaces the saved filter |
| saved filter `open` | accepted; it replaces every saved filter of that field |
| saved filter `locked` | 422 |
| no saved filter, column of the view | accepted and added |
| no saved filter, not a column of the view | 422 |

UserViewFilter.description: A filter sent when executing a view. It has no `user_filter`; sending one is 422.

ViewReference.description: A related record. Filter on it by `id`.

ViewRow.description: The id of the record plus one property per column of the view, in the view's order. Relations are references, dates ISO 8601 in UTC.

data.description: Error details. Validation errors list the messages per field.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired token, or invalid credentials

ValidationFailed.description: The request data is not valid

email: The email field must be a valid email address.

TooManyRequests.description: More than 60 requests in a minute

Forbidden.description: The user can see the resource but is not allowed to change it

example.message: Only the owner of view 7 can change it.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state, such as a title the owner already uses

example.message: You already have a view called "Zebra scanners".

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist, or the user cannot see it

GatewayTimeout.description: The query took longer than the execution timeout (5 seconds) and was stopped

example.message: The view took longer than 5000 ms to run. Add filters to narrow it down.
